subject: Recalculating ticks/labels after using expand on an axis

messages.author: ce5f7e8a5b9ab0de
messages.subject: Recalculating ticks/labels after using expand on an axis
parts:
Hi all,

How do I get the ticks and tick labels to recalculate after using
expand to "stretch" the y-axis? I am using facet_wrap with free y
scales, so I can't just use ylim to increase the y-axis limits.

economics$RandFactor <- c("FactorA","FactorB")
p <- ggplot(economics, aes(x=date, y=psavert))
p + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0.05,0)) + facet_wrap(~
RandFactor, ncol=1, scales="free_y")

If I feel that limiting the plot to the range of the data
"unnecessarily" magnifies fluctuations due to domain knowledge, I can
use the expand function to broaden the y-axis limits. However, the
ticks and tick-labels don't seem to recalculate. To take an extreme
case, let's try it with:

p + geom_point() + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0.05,0)) + facet_wrap(~
RandFactor, ncol=1, scales="free_y")

I get all the tick labels in the center of the plot. How do I get them
to recalculate, so they span the whole (expanded) y-axis?

Many thanks,
Bob

P.S. I understand from the ggplot2 website that the two numbers are a
multiplicative factor and an additive one - does that mean that the
default expand=c(0.05, 0) means 5% padding of the range on each side?
c(1,0) means doubling of the range on both sides (so it's actually
three times the y-range as the original unmodified plot)? And c(0,1)
means increasing the scale by 1 on each side (in the same units as the
data)?

Can you not use expand_limits() for this?

p + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~
RandFactor, ncol=1, scales="free_y") +
scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0)) + expand_limits(y=c(-20,20))

HTH,

baptiste

complex enough to show why I wanted to use expand(). In my dataset,
the two facets have slightly different ranges, so a fixed ylim won't
work. If I can modify my example as follows:
economics$RandFactor <- c("FactorA","FactorB")

economics$psavert[economics$RandFactor == "FactorB"] <-
economics$psavert[economics$RandFactor == "FactorB"] - 30
p <- ggplot(economics, aes(x=date, y=psavert))
p + geom_point() + facet_wrap(~ RandFactor, ncol=1, scales="free_y")

Now you can see that static expanded limits won't work. I want the
data in each facet to be "centered" vertically, but to expand the
y-limits for each facet so that the minor fluctuations in each facet
are visually minimized.

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Recalculating ticks/labels after using expand on an axis
parts:
Hi Bob,

You're using the expand parameter for a purpose it wasn't designed for
- the point of it is to give a little space between the data and the
ticks, so adding ticks in that gap would defeat the purpose. However,
if you look at the source code for expand_limits, you can see
modifying for your needs is pretty simple. You just construct a data
frame that provides both the y values and the facet values and then
use that with geom_blank.

ranges <- data.frame(RandFactor = c("a", "a", "b", "b"), y = c(1, 100,
1000, 10000))
p + geom_blank(aes(y = y), data = ranges, inherit.aes = FALSE)

Hadley
